sources.entry: apsw - Another Python SQLite Wrapper, exposing the complete SQLite C API.

summary.one_liner: APSW ("Another Python SQLite Wrapper") is a Python extension that exposes the complete SQLite C API to Python code, with support for CPython 3.11 onward.
summary.what_it_does: APSW wraps the SQLite C API and Python's C API so that SQLite features can be used directly from Python. The README names full text search, sessions, virtual tables, VFS (virtual file system), JSON, and CArray as supported areas. All functionality is available in regular synchronous code, and the README says there is full support for async frameworks. The README describes APSW as a fuller-featured alternative to the builtin sqlite3 module, which it recommends if you want SQLite to behave like other database drivers. Documentation includes a section on differences between APSW and sqlite3. Releases are published to PyPI and GitHub.
use_cases: Using SQLite full text search from Python
Writing a custom VFS for SQLite file access
Using SQLite from async Python frameworks
Accessing the full SQLite C API from Python
notable: Exposes the complete SQLite C API to Python rather than a subset
Supports virtual tables, VFS, sessions, full text search, and JSON
Works in both synchronous code and async frameworks
Documented differences versus the builtin sqlite3 module
caveats: Supports CPython 3.11 onwards only, per the README
The README recommends the builtin sqlite3 module if you want interchangeable behavior with other database drivers
